title: Consolidate GPU capability mapping and unified runtime fallback matrix
creator: Diego Ramirez
description:
Summary:
This ticket consolidates duplicate and fragmented GPU capability mappings and hard-coded fallback logic across the runtime (device probing, model-to-kernel selection, and quantized-kernel fallbacks). The goal is a single canonical capability matrix and a deterministic fallback decision engine that is small, testable, and independent from multiple ad-hoc probes embedded in different crates and services.

Motivation:
- Recent incidents show inconsistent fallback choices between hosted and dedicated fleets when a newer CUDA/Triton/CUTLASS combo is detected.
- Multiple probe implementations increase maintenance cost and cause subtle discrepancies in kernel selection, contributing to out-of-memory regressions and unexpected performance cliffs.
- Upgrading CUDA/Triton/CUTLASS variants requires repeating compatibility logic changes in several places.

Goals / Acceptance criteria:
1) Introduce a single GPU capability registry (JSON+schema) consumed by runtime components (probe, scheduler, kernel selector).
2) Replace 3 ad-hoc probe implementations with a thin adapter that reads the registry and emits a canonical capability object.
3) Implement a unified fallback matrix (priority-ordered list of compatible kernel variants) alongside a deterministic selection algorithm and public feature flags.
4) All existing unit/integration tests must pass; add regression tests that simulate heterogenous GPU fleets and mixed CUDA/Triton/CUTLASS combos.
5) Deploy as feature-flagged in runtime-1.22 with gradual rollout and automated canary checks (latency and OOM regression detection).

Non-goals:
- This ticket does not add new kernel implementations or change quantization math. It only centralizes mapping and decision logic.

Technical approach:
- Design a compact capability schema (vendor, compute_capability, cuda_version, triton_version, cutlass_family, driver_version_range, quirks) stored under /etc/redwood/gpu_capabilities.json in private deployments and in config service for hosted.
- Build a capability adapter library (Rust, small crate) that normalizes probe outputs and validates them against schema. Expose a stable interface used by: gpu-probe, kernel-selector, and autoscaler.
- Implement the fallback matrix as a JSON file with priority rules and optional cost hints used by the kernel selector. The selector will prefer in-order matches and fall back to the next compatible quant/kernel variant.
- Remove duplicated hard-coded rules scattered across runtime modules and replace with calls to the new adapter. Keep a compatibility shim for one release to avoid API churn.
- Add feature flags: "unified-gpu-matrix" (off by default), "unified-matrix-enforce" (on canaries only).

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for schema validation and selection logic.
- Integration test harness simulating: mixed GPUs (A100/V100/T4), mixed CUDA versions (11.8/12.x/13.x), and Triton/CUTLASS variants to assert deterministic selection.
- Performance benchmark: run 1k short-sequence traces to ensure selection latency < 200µs per request on cold-start path.
- Canary rollout: enable on 1% of traffic in hosted; validate latency, error rate, and OOM; increase to 10% then 50% if no regressions.

Rollout and rollback:
- Merge behind feature flag. Deploy to staging with extensive integration tests.
- Stage -> canary (1% hosted, dedicated test pool) for 48 hours with automated alerts.
- If regressions detected, flip feature flag off (fast rollback).

Migration and compatibility notes:
- Provide a migration script that converts existing probe outputs to the new capability registry format for on-prem customers.
- Keep a lightweight adapter to read legacy env vars and prefer explicit registry when present.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: selector bug causes suboptimal kernel selection leading to high latency or OOM. Mitigation: conservative default fallback, heavy unit/IT tests, and staged canary rollout.
- Risk: schema drift between hosted and private. Mitigation: release a versioned schema and compatibility checker.

Documentation and artifacts:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/Unified+GPU+Capability+Matrix (draft)
- Implementation PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4521 (WIP)
- Migration script PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/tools/pull/187

Estimated effort:
- 8 points (2 engineers, 2 weeks including tests and canary)

Stakeholders:
- Runtime: Morgan Lee (assignee), Amina Kaur (owner)
- Infra: Jesse Patel (review), SRE oncall for canary monitoring

Next steps:
- Finalize schema and land initial crate with unit tests (Morgan).
- Create integration test scenarios and CI jobs (Diego).
- Coordinate canary pool and alerting with SRE (schedulable for 2025-11-22).
